cases.title: “Ask about this” on the Mobile tile
cases.question: What has Brad built on mobile?
cases.answer: Brad has built a range of mobile work across several jobs. At Bleacher Report, Brad built and maintained Android product experiences for a high-traffic sports media platform, across architecture, feature delivery, reliability and release quality. At BookShout, Brad modernized the Android app with Kotlin, Architecture Components, Data Binding, RxJava 2, OkHttp and Retrofit. At Bottle Rocket, Brad shipped native Android apps in Java and Kotlin for brands including Coca-Cola Freestyle, AskPETMD, Starwood SPG and Chewy. At RealPage, Brad led Android development across a suite of real-estate management apps, setting architecture and quality standards and coordinating delivery across mobile products. At Hopper, Brad co-architected and built RemoteUI, a server-driven UI framework rendered natively with Jetpack Compose and MVVM on Android and SwiftUI on iOS. Brad also built VINDecoded's native apps: Re-platformed from AngularJS/Cordova to a React/TypeScript web app, native Android and iOS apps, and a Node.js/TypeScript API.

cases.title: “Ask about this” on the Full-stack tile
cases.question: What has Brad built across the stack?
cases.answer: Brad has built across mobile, web, backend and AI work. On the mobile side, Brad Co-architected and built RemoteUI, a server-driven UI framework rendered natively with Jetpack Compose and MVVM on Android and SwiftUI on iOS, and at Hopper Brad moved to full-stack work across Android, iOS, web front end and backend services, building Android and iOS features in Kotlin and Swift. On the web and backend side, VINDecoded was re-platformed from AngularJS/Cordova to a React/TypeScript web app, native Android and iOS apps, and a Node.js/TypeScript API backed by SQL, Firebase, Azure and cloud analytics. At Hopper, Brad co-developed Scala services and partner API contracts for order confirmation, payment collection, contract creation and persistence, and servicing, including refunds and rebooking. For AI, Brad shipped production AI features: grounded streaming vehicle chat, with provider-switchable models and tool-isolated vehicle data, and vision-based VIN, plate and gas-receipt scanning with structured outputs.

cases.title: “Ask about this” on “Vehicle-history and research platform”
cases.question: Tell me more about this: “A profitable vehicle-history and research platform for shoppers, owners and sellers.”
cases.answer: The phrase comes from Brad's VINDecoded product. A profitable vehicle-history and research platform for shoppers, owners and sellers. VINDecoded turns a VIN or a license plate into what a person needs to know about a car: specs, recalls, market value, the window sticker and its history report. Owners also use it to track maintenance, fuel and recalls, and to read their car through an OBD-II adapter. It is one product on three platforms. A React web app runs in the browser and inside both mobile apps. It earns money from ads, one-time reports, credits and memberships.

Quotas, credits, kill switches, evals and PostHog/Sentry observability guard both. The site also notes that Ask about Brad's API runs on Cloud Run with Hono, and Claude Haiku 5.5 answers. For more on how the evals work, evals put a number on every AI change. Unit tests mock the model, so on their own they can't show that a model swap or a prompt edit made the answers worse. `pnpm eval` runs the production code with a real model on frozen, labelled cases, scores the answers in code rather than with a judging model, and reports accuracy, cost per call and latency.
